questions.q: Two particles of equal mass $m$~move in a circle of radius $r$& under the action of their mutual gravitational attraction. The speed of each particle will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let speed of both the particles be& $v$.

Then, gravitational force between the particles will provide the required centripetal force.

Therefore,

$\dfrac{G\left(m\right)\left(m\right)}{\left(2r\right)2} = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{Gm}{4r}}$

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is $g$. If the diameter of earth reduces to half of its original value and mass remains constant, then acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth would be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity is related to the mass and the radius of the Earth by the formula:

$g = \dfrac{GM}{R2} ⇒ g ∝ \dfrac{1}{R2} . . . \left(1\right)$

Thus, from equation (1), it follows that

\dfrac{g2}{{g}_{1}} = {R}_{1}^{2}{R}_{2}^{2} = {R}_{1}^{2} $\left(\dfrac{R1}{2})2 = 4 ⇒ {g}_{2} = 4g$

questions.q: A body of mass $m$ is projected with velocity $\lambda{v}_{e}$ in vertically upward direction from the surface of the earth into space. It is given that ${v}_{e}$ is escape velocity and $\lambda < 1$. If air resistance is considered to the negligible, then the maximum height from the centre of earth, to which the body can go, will be ($R$ : radius of earth)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Escape velocity is given by,& ${v}_{e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{e}}{Re}}$

If the body goes to the height $h$~from the surface of the earth, using mechanical energy conservation,

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(\lambda\sqrt{\dfrac{2G{M}_{e}}{Re}}\right)2 - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{Re} = - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e} + h}$

$⇒ {λ}^{2}\dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{Re} - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{Re} = - \dfrac{G{M}_{e}m}{{R}_{e} + h}$

$⇒ \left({R}_{e} + h\right) = \dfrac{Re}{1 - {λ}^{2}}$

questions.q: Two identical particles of mass $1$ kg each go round a circle of radius $R$, under the action of their mutual gravitational attraction. The angular speed of each particle is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$F = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{( 2R{)}^{2}} = mR{ω}^{2}$

$\omega = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{G}{R3}}$

questions.q: If a satellite orbiting the Earth is 9 times closer to the Earth than the Moon, what is the time period of rotation of the satellite? Given rotational time period of Moon $=27$ days and gravitational attraction between the satellite and the moon is neglected.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}^2 \propto \mathrm{R}^3 \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{m}}}{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{s}}}\right)^2=\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R} / 9}\right)^3 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{m}}}{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{s}}}=(3)^3 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{s}}=\left(\frac{27}{27}\right)=1 \text { day }\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A test particle is moving in a circular orbit in the gravitational field produced by a mass density $ρ\left(r\right) = \dfrac{K}{r^{2}} .$ Identify the current relation between the radius $R$ of the particle’s orbit and its period $T:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$M = ∫ ρ4\pir^{2}dr$
$= {∫}_{0}^{R}\dfrac{K}{r^{2}}4\pir^{2}dr$
$= 4\piKR$
Satellite velocity $= \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R}} = \sqrt{4\piK}$
Time period, $T = \dfrac{2\piR}{v} = \dfrac{2\piR}{\sqrt{4\piK}}$
Now,
$\dfrac{T}{R} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{4\piK}} =$ constant

questions.q: The value of the acceleration due to gravity is ${g}_{1}$ at a height $h = \dfrac{R}{2}$~($R =$ radius of the earth) from the surface of the earth. It is again equal to ${g}_{1}$ at a depth $d$ below the surface the earth. The ratio  \left(\dfrac{d}{R}\right)$ equals:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that

${g}_{n} = {g}_{d}$

$\dfrac{GM}{( R + h{)}^{2}} = \dfrac{GM}{R3} ( R - d )$

$\dfrac{GM}{( R + R / 2{)}^{2}} = \dfrac{GM}{R3} ( R - d )$

$\dfrac{4GM}{9R^{2}} = \dfrac{GM}{R2} \left($1 - $\dfrac{d}{R}\right)

\dfrac{4}{9} =$1 - $\dfrac{d}{R}

\dfrac{d}{R} =$1 - $\dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{5}{9}

$d = $\dfrac{5}{9}$R$

$

questions.q: The gravitational potential at a point above the surface of earth is $- 5 . 12 \times {10}^{7}J{kg}^{- 1}$ and the acceleration due to gravity at that point is $6 . 4ms^{- 2}$. Assume that the mean radius of earth to be $6400$ km. The height of this point above the earth's surface is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Gravitational potential at a distance $r$ from the centre of the earth is given by, $V = \dfrac{- GM}{r}$.

Therefore, we can write

$- \dfrac{G{M}_{E}}{{R}_{E} + h} = - 5 . 12 \times {10}^{7} \ldots \left(i\right)$

also acceleration due to gravity at that point will be

\dfrac{G{M}_{E}}{ \left({R}_{E} + h\right)2} =$6 . 4 \ldots \left(ii\right)$

By (i) and (ii), we get

$\dfrac{- \dfrac{G{M}_{E}}{{R}_{E} + h}}{G{M}_{E}\left({R}_{E} + h\right)2} = \dfrac{5 . 12 \times {10}^{7}}{6 . 4}$

$⇒ {R}_{E} + h = 80 \times {10}^{5}m = 8000km ⇒ h = 8000km - 6400km = 1600km$

questions.q: A satellite is launched into a circular orbit of radius ' R ' around the earth. A second satellite is launched into an orbit of radius 1.03 R . The time period of revolution of the second satellite is larger than the first one approximately by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $T_1 \propto(R)^{3 / 2}$ and $T_2 \propto(1.03 R)^{3 / 2}\Rightarrow \quad T_2=(1.03 R)^{3 / 2} \cdot T_1 \approx 1.045 T_1$ So $T_2$ will larger by $4.5 \%$ w.r.t. $T_1$.

questions.q: The masses and radii of the earth and moon are  \left({M}_{1}, {R}_{1}\right)$ and  \left({M}_{2}, {R}_{2}\right)$ respectively. Their centres are at a distance $r$~apart. Find the minimum escape velocity for a particle of mass $m$ & to be projected from the middle of these two masses :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
On conserving mechanical energy. The initial total energy is& equal to final total energy, $⇒ - \left(\dfrac{G{M}_{1}}{\dfrac{r}{2}} + \dfrac{G{M}_{2}}{r2}\right)m + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_e^{2} = 0$
$⇒ {v}_{e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4G\left({M}_{1} + {M}_{2}\right)}{r}}$.&

questions.q: If $V$ is the gravitational potential due to sphere of uniform density on its surface, then its value at the centre of sphere will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnitude of gravitational potential of a solid sphere at a distance& $r$~from the centre is~

$V = \dfrac{- GM}{2R^{3}} ( 3R^{2} - r^{2} )$

At~$r = R$,~$V = \dfrac{- GM}{R}$.

At~$r = 0$,~$V ' = \dfrac{- GM}{2R^{3}} ( 3R^{2} ) = \dfrac{- 3GM}{2R}$

Clearly,~$V ' = \dfrac{3V}{2}$.

questions.q: If the angular momentum of a planet of mass $m,$ moving around the Sun in a circular orbit is $L,$ about the center of the Sun, its areal velocity is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{dA} = \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{v}dt$

$\dfrac{d\overset{→}{A}}{dt} =$ areal velocity $= \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{v}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\overset{→}{r} \times m\overset{→}{v}}{m} = \dfrac{1}{2m}L$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{L}{2m}$

questions.q: Two satellites $A$ and $B$ having masses in the ratio $4: 3$ are revolving in circular orbits of radii $3r$ and $4r$ respectively around the earth. The ratio of total mechanical energy of $A$ to $B$ is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that $\dfrac{m1}{m2} = \dfrac{4}{3}, \dfrac{r1}{r2} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Now the total energy of a satellite~$TE = \dfrac{1}{2}m{vo}^{2} + \left(\dfrac{- GMm}{r}\right)

Since the orbital speed of a satellite~${v}_{o} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}

$⇒ TE = - $\dfrac{GMm}{2r}$∝ $\dfrac{m}{r}

$⇒ \dfrac{T{E}_{1}}{T{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{m1}{{m}_{2}} \cdot \dfrac{r2}{r1} = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{16}{9}$

$

questions.q: The ratio of the weights of a body on Earth’s surface to that on the surface of a planet is $9: 4$ The mass of the planet is $\dfrac{1}{9}th$ of that of the Earth. If $R$ is the radius of the Earth, what is the radius of the planet? (Take the planets to have the same mass density)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Weight $= m \left(\dfrac{GM}{R^{2}}\right)
$∴ $\dfrac{9}{4} = \dfrac{G{M}_{e}}{{R}_e^{2}} \times \dfrac{{R}_p^{2}}{G{M}_{p}}
Given that,~${M}_{p} = $\dfrac{{M}_{e}}{9}
$∴ $\dfrac{9}{4} = \dfrac{{M}_{e}}{\left(\dfrac{{M}_{e}}{9}\right)} \times \dfrac{{R}_p^{2}}{{R}_e^{2}}
${R}_p^{2} = {R}_e^{2} $\times \dfrac{1}{4}
${R}_{p} = $\dfrac{{R}_{e}}{2}
As,~${R}_{e} = R$
$⇒ {R}_{p} = \dfrac{R}{2}$

$

questions.q: Four identical particles of mass $m$ are kept at the four corners of a square. If the gravitational force exerted on one of the masses by the other masses is \left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2} + 1}{32}\right)\dfrac{Gm^{2}}{L2}$, the length of the sides of the square is$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resultant force, ${F}_{net} = \sqrt{2}F + F '$, where

$F = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{a2}$ and $F ' = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{\left(\sqrt{2}a\right)2}$

Therefore, ${F}_{net} = \sqrt{2}\dfrac{Gm^{2}}{a2} + \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{2a^{2}}$

Comparing with the expression given in the question, we get

\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2} + 1}{32}\right)\dfrac{Gm^{2}}{L2} = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{a^{2}} \left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2} + 1}{2}\right)

$⇒ a = 4L$

questions.q:
A body weighs $49N$ on a spring balance at the north pole. What will be its weight recorded on the same weighing machine, if it is shifted to the equator?

[Use $g = \dfrac{GM}{R2} = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$~and radius of earth, $R = 6400km .$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Weight of pole $= mg = 49N$

At equator due to rotation~$= {g}_{e} = g - R{ω}^{2}$

so~$W = m{g}_{e} = m \left(g - R{ω}^{2}\right)$

$∴ {W}_{P} > {W}_{e}$~${W}_{p} = 49N$

So,~${W}_{e} = 48 . 83N .$~${W}_{e} < 49N

$

questions.q: The time period of a satellite revolving around earth in a given orbit is $7$ hours. If the radius of orbit is increased to three times its previous value, then approximate new time period of the satellite will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From& Kepler's Third Law(The Law of Periods), we know

$T^{2} ∝ R^{3} ⇒ {T}_{2}^{2}{T}_{1}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{R2}{R1}\right)3 = \left(\dfrac{3R}{R}\right)3$

Therefore,~${T}_{2} = \sqrt{27}{T}_{1}$

$= 5 . 19 \times 7 \approx 36hours$

questions.q: Four identical particles of mass $M$ are located at the corners of a square of side $‘a’$ . What should be their speed if each of them revolves under the influence of other’s gravitational field in a circular orbit circumscribing the square?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Gravitational force on each mass 'M'
$= \sqrt{2}\dfrac{GM^{2}}{a^{2}} + \dfrac{GM^{2}}{{\left(\sqrt{2}a\right)}^{2}} = \left(\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\dfrac{GM^{2}}{a^{2}}$
This force will provide required centripetal force
\left(\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\dfrac{GM^{2}}{a^{2}} = \dfrac{Mv^{2}}{( a / \sqrt{2} )}$
$v = \sqrt{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)\dfrac{GM}{a}} = 1.16\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{a}}

questions.q: The radius in kilometer to which the present radius of earth $( R = 6400km )$ to be compressed so that the escape velocity is increased $10$ time is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${V}_{e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Gm}{R}} \ldots \left(1\right)$

$10{V}_{e} = $\sqrt{\dfrac{2Gm}{R '}} \ldots \left(2\right)$

questions.q: Two satellites ${S}_{1}$ and ${S}_{2}$ are revolving in circular orbits around a planet with radius ${R}_{I} = 3200km$ and ${R}_{2} = 800km$ respectively. The ratio of speed of satellite ${S}_{1}$ to the speed of satellite ${S}_{2}$ in their respective orbits would be $\dfrac{1}{x}$ where $x =$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Orbital velocity of a satellite in circular motion around a planet,

${v}_{o} = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R}} ∝ \dfrac{1}{R}$

Now,~$\dfrac{v1}{v2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{R2}{R1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{800}{3200}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, the value of~$x = 2$.

questions.q: Acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is ' $g$ '. If the diameter of earth is reduced to one third of its original value and mass remains unchanged, then the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is $\ldots\ldots$ g.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\because$ acceleration due to gravity on surface is given by
$\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}^2}$ Now since diameter is reduced to $1 / 3^{\text {rd }}$, radius also reduces to $1 / 3^{\text {rd }}$, keeping mass constant
New value of acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is
$\mathrmg^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}{3}\right)^2}=9 \frac{\mathrm{GMe}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}^2}=9 \mathrm{~g}$

${g}_{A} = {g}_{C}$

so~$OA = \dfrac{4R}{9}; AB = R - r = \dfrac{5R}{9}$

$OA: AB = 4: 5$

The planet $B$ is $4 \sqrt{2}$ times more massive than planet $A$. The ratio  \left(\frac{L_B}{L_A}\right)$ of angular momentum  \left(L_B\right)$ of planet $B$ to that of planet $A  \left(L_A\right) is closest to integer ________.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{mv}_0 $\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{m}$ \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}}} $\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{m}$ \sqrt{\mathrm{GMR}}$
here M is mass of star
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{~L}_{\mathrm{A}}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{A}}} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}} \\
& =4 \sqrt{2} \sqrt{\frac{2}{1}} \\
& \frac{\mathrm{~L}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{~L}_{\mathrm{A}}}=8
